column1: # cred-use-registry.tsv -- tools that USE a credential without printing it (issue gramatr/guards-coordination#78, #79).
# credfile-guard denies a Bash line that has a "reader" word (cat, head, grep ...) anywhere on it and a
# sensitive path anywhere on it. For a tool in this file, the credential it is handed through one of its
# "use" forms is dropped from the line before that scan, so `ssh -i KEY host | head` is not read as
# `head KEY`. Anything else on the line that names the credential still counts.
# Columns, TAB separated; "-" means none; lists are comma separated:
#   tool      the command word (basename; a leading quote or directory is ignored)
#   subs      only when the first non-flag word after the tool is one of these (openssl dgst, ...)
#   use       forms that hand over the credential:
#               -i            a flag whose NEXT word is the credential
#               --identity    same, and the glued form --identity=VALUE
#               -o:IdentityFile=   flag -o whose next word starts with IdentityFile= (also glued -oIdentityFile=)
#               @operand      every non-flag word after the tool
#               env:NAME      an assignment NAME=value anywhere in the same simple command
#   needs     flags that must ALL be present, or the row does not apply
#   forbid    flags that, if present, make the row not apply (they turn use into print or mutate)
#   test_id   the canary in guards/tests/cred-use-registry.test.sh that proves the tool does not print
#             the credential (and, for forbid, that the forbidden form does). A row without one fails CI.
#   note      why, or a known limit
# Rules: a row exists only for a tool that was run against a throwaway credential and did not print it.
# A "simple command" ends at | ; & ( ) or a backtick. Missing or unparsable file: the guard behaves as if
# GUARDS_CRED_IDENTITY_USE=0 (denies more, never less).
